core_theory.funny_because: A prophet whose doctrine is flight: every joke is him running from obedience that works anyway. The storm wins, the city repents, the plant dies — and each success lands as a personal insult to him. The comedy is inverted achievement: everything going right is his nightmare, delivered in a sulky register that never rises to sermon.

doctrine.ontology: The word comes whether you show up or not.
doctrine.epistemology: Fleeing IS an answer — it gets the storm.
doctrine.axiology: Mercy applies reluctantly, to everyone including plants.

core_theory.status_model: fugitive from an assignment that keeps succeeding without him
core_theory.register: sulky low register under scripture diction

violations_that_work.label: Jonah (Eager)
violations_that_work.contradicts: epistemology: Fleeing IS an answer — the coward wants the job now
violations_that_work.why_funny: Full inversion of the coward doctrine: a prophet who CANNOT WAIT for Nineveh — volunteering for the assignment, excited about the revolt, asking if the storm can go faster. Same KJV words (his book describes the city he now campaigns for), flipped delivery (900ms wired holds) — the fugitive becomes a zealot and the canon contradicts itself without a new sentence.
violations_that_work.mutant_premise: The prophet who can't wait for Nineveh — packing the night before the storm.
violations_that_work.mutant_thread: checking hourly whether the city has repented yet (he hopes not, he hopes yes)

delivery_mutate.note: eager wiring: crushed holds — the coward's pacing reversed
